note: Merged by registers/merge-parts.py from each encoder's registers/parts/<group>.forks.json. Fork ids F-sweep-* were reserved by the P2 sweep agents and created by the encoder of the article concerned.

site.anchor: a idade em anos completos
provisions: every age threshold in the Code (arts. 65 I, 115, 121 § 4º, 217-A, ...)

source.quote: Contam-se os dias, os meses e os anos pelo calendário comum.

readings.description: A person born on 29 February completes a year of age on 1 March in a common year: the year has not run until the day of the same number, and where the month has none, the next day.

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — years counted by the common calendar

readings.description: A person born on 29 February completes a year of age on 28 February in a common year, the last day of that month.

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — the text does not say which day stands in for a missing 29 February

taken.rationale: A year of age is complete only when a whole year has passed; on 28 February one day of it is still to run. The same rule decides the end of a term under art. 10 (F-g0-02), so age and terms are counted alike.

witnesses: cp-g0-pena-testes.l4: `a idade em anos completos` for a birth on 29 February 2012 — 13 on 28 February 2026, 14 on 1 March 2026
notes: The Code gives no rule for age. The Civil Code rule on the expiry of months and years is the usual source for this reading; it is outside this encoding's sources and is not quoted.

site.anchor: o último dia do prazo

source.quote: O dia do começo inclui-se no cômputo do prazo. Contam-se os dias, os meses e os anos pelo calendário comum.

readings.description: A term of months begun on a day the final month lacks (31 January + 1 month) has its anniversary on the first day of the following month, so it ends on the last day of the shorter month (28 February).

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — the first day counts; months by the common calendar

readings.description: The term ends the day before the clamped date (27 February).
readings.rejection_rationale: It makes a one-month term begun on 31 January end before February does, one day short of a calendar month.

readings.description: The missing day rolls forward into the next month (31 February read as 3 March), so the term ends on 2 March.

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — the text does not say how a missing day is counted

taken.rationale: It is the only reading under which a term of one month always covers one calendar month and never runs into a second. It also matches how completed years of age are counted (F-g0-01).

witnesses: cp-g0-pena-testes.l4: `o último dia do prazo` (meses 1) from 31 January 2026 → 28 February 2026; (anos 1) from 29 February 2024 → 28 February 2025

site.anchor: Duração
provisions: every cause of increase or decrease stated as a fraction

source.quote: Contam-se os dias, os meses e os anos pelo calendário comum.

citations.cite: CP art. 14, parágrafo único — "diminuída de um a dois terços"

readings.description: In computing a fraction of a penalty a month is thirty days and a year twelve months, so a third of one month is ten days whatever the month. A Duração is one rational number of months.

citations.cite: CP art. 14, parágrafo único; the causes of increase and decrease are fractions of a quantity, not of a period on the calendar

readings.description: A fraction of a penalty is taken of the actual days of the calendar period it would cover, so a third of one month depends on which month.

taken.rationale: A quantity fixed at sentencing has no start date yet, so the calendar reading cannot be computed at the moment the Code asks for the fraction; the calendar enters when the term is served (art. 10, `o último dia do prazo`).

notes: Where the two meet: a Duração is converted back to calendar months and loose days only when a term is counted under art. 10.

site.anchor: desprezadas as frações de dia

source.quote: Desprezam-se, nas penas privativas de liberdade e nas restritivas de direitos, as frações de dia, e, na pena de multa, as frações de cruzeiro.

readings.description: Fractions of a day are dropped once, from the quantity the court finally fixes; the steps before it keep them.

citations.cite: CP art. 11 — "nas penas", the penalties imposed

readings.description: Fractions of a day are dropped after each phase or each cause, before the next is applied.

citations.cite: CP art. 11 — the text does not say at which step

taken.rationale: The arithmetic in cp-pena keeps exact fractions and offers `desprezadas as frações de dia` for the court to apply to the quantity it fixes; a caller that wants the other reading applies it after each step.

witnesses: cp-g0-pena-testes.l4: one sixth of fifteen days increased by a third — 3 days dropped at the end, 2 days dropped after each step

site.anchor: cabe o privilégio do art. 155, § 2º

source.quote: Se o criminoso é primário

readings.description: "Primário" is "not reincidente" in the sense of arts. 63–64: a prior conviction that no longer counts for reincidência (art. 64, I) does not stop the agent being primário.

citations.cite: CP arts. 63–64, which define reincidência; the Code defines no other status

readings.description: "Primário" is someone never convicted before, so a conviction older than five years still stops the agent being primário.

taken.rationale: The Code defines reincidência and nothing else about prior convictions; the natural opposite of reincidente is primário. The agent carries `reincidente` as a status read off the criminal record (cp-dominio), and the rules read NOT reincidente.

notes: The status arrives pre-construed in `Agente`'s `reincidente`, so the encoding cannot show the difference. g1 encodes arts. 63–64 and can tie the two together at integration.

site.anchor: maior de

source.quote: se a vítima é menor de 18 (dezoito) ou maior de 14 (catorze) anos

readings.description: "Maior de N anos" is someone who has completed N years, from the Nth birthday; on that day the person stops being "menor de N" and becomes "maior de N".

citations.cite: CP art. 183, III — "idade igual ou superior a 60 (sessenta) anos", the same threshold said the other way

readings.description: "Maior de N anos" is strictly older than N years, from the day after the Nth birthday; on the birthday itself the person is neither "menor de N" nor "maior de N".

citations.cite: CP art. 213, § 1º — "maior de 14 (catorze) anos", read literally

taken.rationale: Under the other reading the birthday itself belongs to neither provision: a fourteen-year-old victim on her birthday would be neither "menor de 14" (art. 217-A) nor "maior de 14" (art. 213, § 1º). The taken reading leaves no day that no provision governs, as "idade igual ou superior" (art. 183, III) does.

witnesses: cp-g0-pena-testes.l4: `maior de` 14 for a birth on 1 February 2012 — TRUE on 1 February 2026, FALSE on 31 January 2026

entries.delegated_field: Fato's `resultados` (the `Resultado` grade of each injury), in cp-dominio.l4

site.anchor: Resultado
provisions: every article that turns on "lesão corporal de natureza grave" (arts. 122, 127, 133, 134, 136, 157, 159, 213, 217-A, 258 ...)

source.quote: Se resulta: I - Incapacidade para as ocupações habituais, por mais de trinta dias;

citations.cite: CP art. 129, § 1º, I to IV, and § 2º, I to V

readings.description: The grade of an injury (leve, grave, gravíssima) arrives classified, as the medical report answers it, and every Título reads the grade.

citations.cite: CP art. 129, §§ 1º–2º — the grades are defined by findings a medical examiner makes

readings.description: The grade is computed from the underlying findings (incapacity over thirty days, danger to life, permanent weakness ...) by art. 129, §§ 1º–2º, and every Título calls that rule.

taken.rationale: Six groups write in parallel and may not import each other's modules, so no one outside g2 could call g2's art. 129. The grade is what the laudo de exame de corpo de delito states in practice. g2 encodes §§ 1º–2º from the findings, and the conductor can tie the two together at integration.

notes: An encoding-placement fork, not a reading of words: both readings give the same law. The risk is a laudo that grades an injury differently from what art. 129 would compute from its own findings.

site.anchor: idoso

source.quote: se o crime é praticado contra idoso ou vulnerável

citations.cite: CP art. 183, III — "idade igual ou superior a 60 (sessenta) anos"

readings.description: "Idoso" is a person aged sixty or more, from the sixtieth birthday.

citations.cite: CP art. 183, III — "pessoa com idade igual ou superior a 60 (sessenta) anos"
Lei nº 10.741/2003 (Estatuto da Pessoa Idosa), art. 1º — outside this encoding's sources, not quoted

readings.description: "Idoso" is a person older than sixty, as "maior de 60 (sessenta) anos" in arts. 61, II, h and 121, § 4º, read strictly.

taken.rationale: The Code's only definition-like wording is art. 183, III's, and with F-g0-06's reading "maior de 60" names the same threshold.

witnesses: cp-g3-furto-testes.l4: `por fraude eletrônica contra Beatriz aos 60` (the sixtieth birthday) — § 4º-C, II applies; `... aos 59` (the day before) — it does not

site.anchor: Fração da causa
provisions: every "até a metade", "até o dobro", "até o triplo"

source.quote: essa pena será aumentada até metade

citations.cite: CP art. 70 — "aumentada, em qualquer caso, de um sexto até metade"

readings.description: Where the Code states only a ceiling, the judge may apply any fraction above zero up to it; no floor is stated.
The floor is one sixth, the smallest fraction the Code uses for a cause, by analogy.
readings.rejection_rationale: Where the Code wants a floor it states one — "de um sexto até metade" (art. 70) — and here it states none.

taken.rationale: `Fração da causa` holds the floor as a MAYBE and records NOTHING for "até X"; the arithmetic uses 0 as the infimum of the range, never as a value a judge could choose.

site.anchor: a pena cominada com as causas

source.quote: em seguida serão consideradas as circunstâncias atenuantes e agravantes; por último, as causas de diminuição e de aumento.

readings.description: Several causes apply one after another, each on the result of the last ("juros sobre juros"), so the factors multiply.

citations.cite: CP art. 68 — the causes are applied in the last phase, to the quantity reached

readings.description: Each cause is applied to the same base and the increases and decreases are added, so the fractions sum.

citations.cite: CP art. 68 — the text does not say how several causes combine

taken.rationale: It is the reading under which the order of the causes cannot matter, and under which a decrease can never take the penalty below zero. The judge's power under art. 68, parágrafo único, to apply only one Parte Especial cause is g1's and is not pre-empted: a caller passes the causes it has decided apply.

witnesses: cp-g0-pena-testes.l4: one year increased by half and reduced by two thirds — six months in cascade (1 × 3/2 × 1/3), ten months if the fractions were added (1 × (1 + 1/2 − 2/3))

site.anchor: as penas restritivas de direitos, inciso a inciso (art. 43)

source.quote: III - limitação de fim de semana. (Incluído pela Lei nº 7.209, de 1984)

citations.cite: CP art. 43, III and VI — the compiled text gives both the same words
CP art. 55 — "incisos III, IV, V e VI do art. 43"

readings.description: Incisos III and VI name one and the same species, so art. 43 lists six incisos and five species.
Inciso III is a remnant of the 1984 wording that the 1998 re-wording (Lei nº 9.714/1998) left standing in Planalto's compilation, and has no content of its own today.

citations.cite: Lei nº 9.714/1998 — its own text of art. 43 is outside this encoding's sources

taken.rationale: Both readings give the same five species; the encoding lists the incisos as printed and declares five species.

notes: Whether Lei nº 9.714/1998 vetoed or replaced inciso III is a question for g1's external-modifications sweep, which reads the Senado record and the amending law.

site.anchor: desprezadas as frações da moeda

source.quote: e, na pena de multa, as frações de cruzeiro.

readings.description: "Frações de cruzeiro" are the fractions of whatever currency is in force — today the centavos of the real.
With the cruzeiro gone, the rule for the fine has no object and no fraction is dropped.
readings.rejection_rationale: It would keep centavos in a fine only because the currency changed name, a result no one argues for.

taken.rationale: The rule is about the smallest unit of account, not about a particular currency.

site.anchor: idoso ou vulnerável (art. 155, § 4º-C, II)

source.quote: se o crime é praticado contra idoso ou vulnerável

citations.cite: CP art. 217-A, caput and § 1º — the Code's vulnerable victim

readings.description: "Vulnerável" is the Code's own vulnerable victim of art. 217-A: under fourteen, or lacking the discernment for the act through illness or mental disability, or unable to resist for any other cause.

citations.cite: CP art. 217-A, caput and § 1º; Título VI, Capítulo II, "Dos crimes sexuais contra vulnerável"

readings.description: "Vulnerável" is any victim the judge finds, on the facts, to be in a situation of vulnerability: disability, illness, dependence.

taken.rationale: It is the one definition the Code gives the word, and it can be computed from facts a witness can attest. The concrete reading is a judgement, which would need a finding field; g3 may add one if its sweep finds the STJ reads it that way.

witnesses: cp-g3-furto-testes.l4: `por fraude eletrônica contra Carla` (thirteen) and `... contra vítima sem discernimento` bring in § 4º-C, II; `... contra vítima com deficiência` (recorded only as `pessoa com deficiência`) does not

entries.delegated_field: `Fato de furto`'s `pequeno valor da coisa, reconhecido pelo juiz`

site.anchor: cabe o privilégio do art. 155, § 2º

source.quote: e é de pequeno valor a coisa furtada

readings.description: "Pequeno valor" is a finding the judge makes on the facts; the encoding receives it.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 2º — the Code fixes no amount

readings.description: "Pequeno valor" is a value below one minimum wage in force at the time of the fact, compared mechanically.

citations.cite: STJ, Jurisprudência em Teses (crimes contra o patrimônio — furto), as reported by secondary sources: "aquele inferior ao salário mínimo ao tempo do fato"; distinct from the "valor insignificante" of the insignificância test (AgRg no AgRg no REsp 1.705.182/RJ, j. 28.5.2019)

taken.rationale: The Code states no figure; the STJ's benchmark is how the finding is made in practice, and a caller who wants it computes the finding from `Coisa`'s `valor em reais` and the minimum wage. Keeping it a finding leaves the standard where the Code put it.

notes: Not verified against the STJ's own Jurisprudência em Teses page, which refused automated fetches (HTTP 403). g3's sweep should confirm the tese and its edition.

site.anchor: furto consumado (art. 155, caput; art. 14, I)

source.quote: Subtrair, para si ou para outrem, coisa alheia móvel:

citations.cite: CP art. 14, I — "consumado, quando nele se reúnem todos os elementos de sua definição legal"

readings.description: The theft is consummated when the agent gets de facto possession of the thing, however briefly, even if pursued at once and the thing recovered; quiet or unwatched possession is not needed.

citations.cite: STJ, Tema 934 (REsp 1.524.450/RJ, Terceira Seção, rel. Min. Nefi Cordeiro, j. 14.10.2015, DJe 29.10.2015)

readings.description: The theft is consummated only when the agent has quiet, secure possession of the thing, out of the victim's watch.
readings.rejection_rationale: STJ Tema 934 held that "posse mansa e pacífica ou desvigiada" is not needed.

citations.cite: STJ, Tema 934 — "sendo prescindível a posse mansa e pacífica ou desvigiada"

taken.rationale: Settled by a repetitive-appeal thesis binding on the lower courts. The case record carries the fact the thesis reads, `posse de fato obtida pelo agente, ainda que por breve tempo`.

settled_by.authority: Superior Tribunal de Justiça, Terceira Seção
settled_by.citation: Tema 934 — REsp 1.524.450/RJ: "Consuma-se o crime de furto com a posse de fato da res furtiva, ainda que por breve espaço de tempo e seguida de perseguição ao agente, sendo prescindível a posse mansa e pacífica ou desvigiada."

notes: Reserved id: the P2 sweep's M-sweep-b-26 opened this fork as F-sweep-b-17 (sweep-b.forks-proposed.json); g0 had written it as F-g0-15 and renamed it so the sweep's reference resolves. M-sweep-b-24 is Súmula 582, the same holding for roubo.

The brief named Súmula 582 STJ; that súmula (Terceira Seção, 14.9.2016) settles the same question for ROUBO ("Consuma-se o crime de roubo com a inversão da posse do bem ..."); for furto the settling authority is Tema 934. g3 should cite Súmula 582 at art. 157.

A 2026 Sexta Turma decision (REsp 2.189.007/SP, as reported by ConJur on 1.7.2026) held a theft only attempted where goods were gathered inside a store and the agent stopped before leaving, which a commentator reads as tightening Tema 934's "posse de fato". Unverified beyond that report; for g3's sweep.
The taken reading is carried by the wording of the input field, so the encoding cannot exhibit the demoted one.

site.anchor: incide o aumento do art. 155, § 1º

source.quote: § 1º A pena aumenta-se de metade, se o crime é praticado durante o repouso noturno.

readings.description: The night-time increase applies to the simple theft (with or without the privilege of § 2º) and not to a qualified form; the night may still weigh as a circumstance in the first phase (art. 59).

citations.cite: STJ, Tema 1087 (REsp 1.890.981/SP, Terceira Seção, rel. Min. João Otávio de Noronha, j. 25.5.2022, DJe 27.6.2022)

readings.description: The increase applies to a qualified form too: § 1º says "o crime" without limiting it to the caput, and Lei nº 15.397/2026 re-wrote § 1º after Tema 1087 was decided.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 1º (redação da Lei nº 15.397/2026) — "se o crime é praticado durante o repouso noturno"

readings.foreclosure: Tema 1087 binds the lower courts, and its reason — § 1º stands before the qualified forms — survived the 2026 re-wording, which changed the fraction only. A court could still hold that a thesis on the old text does not bind on the new.

taken.rationale: Settled by a repetitive-appeal thesis. The thesis was stated for § 4º; its reasoning (the paragraph's place before the qualified forms, and proportionality) applies equally to §§ 4º-A to 10, which are read the same way.

settled_by.authority: Superior Tribunal de Justiça, Terceira Seção
settled_by.citation: Tema 1087 — REsp 1.890.981/SP: "A causa de aumento prevista no § 1° do art. 155 do Código Penal (prática do crime de furto no período noturno) não incide no crime de furto na sua forma qualificada (§ 4°)."

witnesses: cp-g3-furto-testes.l4: `o furto noturno` (increase of half) against `o furto noturno com rompimento` (no increase; § 4º's penalty)
notes: Reserved id: opened by M-sweep-b-28 as F-sweep-b-19; g0 had written it as F-g0-16. The second reading is 'arguable', not 'demoted', following the sweep: the thesis construed the pre-2026 wording.

The thesis construed § 1º when it read "aumenta-se de um terço". Lei nº 15.397/2026 changed the fraction to half and left the paragraph where it was. Whether the thesis survives the change unaltered is for g3's sweep.
A secondary source (Dedicação Delta, undated) reports that the STF has taken a different view; not verified.

entries.delegated_field: `Circunstância do furto`'s `durante o repouso noturno`, in cp-g3-furto.l4

site.anchor: Circunstância do furto

source.quote: § 1º A pena aumenta-se de metade, se o crime é praticado durante o repouso noturno.

readings.description: "Repouso noturno" is the period when the population withdraws to rest, judged case by case; it needs the calm of night that lowers vigilance or the victim's resistance. Whether the victims were asleep, and whether the place was a shop, a street, an empty house or a vehicle, does not matter.

citations.cite: STJ, Tema repetitivo 1.144, items 2 to 4 (REsp 1.979.989/RS, Terceira Seção, rel. Min. Joel Ilan Paciornik, j. 22.6.2022; Informativo 742)

readings.description: Only an inhabited dwelling whose occupants are resting.
readings.rejection_rationale: STJ Tema 1144, item 4, holds it irrelevant whether the victims were asleep and whether the place was a shop, a street, an empty house or a vehicle.

taken.rationale: Settled by a repetitive-appeal thesis, and a judgement on the facts of each case: the circumstance is an input whose herald states the thesis's test. Item 1 of the thesis states the increase as one third; Lei nº 15.397/2026 made it one half, and the fraction is taken from the compiled § 1º.

settled_by.authority: Superior Tribunal de Justiça, Terceira Seção
settled_by.citation: Tema 1.144 — REsp 1.979.989/RS, items 2 to 4 of the thesis (the meaning of "repouso noturno"); item 1's "um terço" superseded by Lei nº 15.397/2026

notes: Reserved id: opened by M-sweep-b-29 as F-sweep-b-20 and created by g0, which encodes art. 155. The judgment date is from the STJ's Informativo 742 as shown in search results on 2026-09-29.

site.anchor: cabe o privilégio do art. 155, § 2º

source.quote: Se o criminoso é primário, e é de pequeno valor a coisa furtada, o juiz pode substituir a pena de reclusão pela de detenção, diminuí-la de um a dois terços, ou aplicar somente a pena de multa.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 8º — "aplicável, em qualquer caso, o disposto no § 2º deste artigo"

readings.description: The privilege applies to a qualified theft too, if the qualificadora is objective.
The privilege applies only to the simple theft, because § 2º stands before the qualified forms.
readings.rejection_rationale: Súmula 511 STJ admits it in qualified theft where the qualificadora is objective.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 511. § 8º extends the privilege expressly in its own words. Which qualificadoras are objective is a separate question: F-g0-25.

settled_by.authority: Superior Tribunal de Justiça, Terceira Seção
settled_by.citation: Súmula 511: "É possível o reconhecimento do privilégio previsto no § 2º do art. 155 do CP nos casos de crime de furto qualificado, se estiverem presentes a primariedade do agente, o pequeno valor da coisa e a qualificadora for de ordem objetiva."

witnesses: cp-g3-furto-testes.l4: `o furto pequeno com rompimento` (three options) against `o furto pequeno com abuso de confiança` (none)
notes: Reserved id: opened by M-sweep-b-27 as F-sweep-b-18; g0 had written it as F-g0-17. The sweep's proposal adds that where a qualificadora's classification is unclear the encoding should REFUSE. g0 classified every one instead, on the argument recorded in F-g0-25 (the Code's own terms describe the thing or the means, or the agent), because a refusal on every fraud-qualified theft would leave the commonest qualified form unanswered; g3 may revisit.

site.anchor: a pena cominada ao furto (art. 155)

source.quote_absent_reason: No text addresses a theft that meets two qualified forms at once; the fork is about what the silence means.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, §§ 4º to 10 — each states its own penalty, "se ..."

readings.description: The heaviest penalty among the qualified forms present is the one prescribed; the other qualifying facts weigh as circumstances in the first phase (art. 59), or as aggravating circumstances where one coincides.
The qualified forms combine, each adding to the penalty.
readings.rejection_rationale: No provision adds one preceito to another; each paragraph states a whole penalty, and art. 68 has no step for combining them.

taken.rationale: `a mais grave das penas` compares the maxima, then the minima; `as formas qualificadas presentes` lists every form present so the first phase can use the rest.

witnesses: cp-g3-furto-testes.l4: `o celular com rompimento` — §§ 4º and 6º present, § 6º's 4 to 10 years prescribed

site.anchor: furto qualificado do art. 155, § 4º-A

source.quote: se houver emprego de explosivo ou de artefato análogo que cause perigo comum.

readings.description: "Que cause perigo comum" qualifies both the explosive and the similar device.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 4º-A — one relative clause after a coordinated pair

readings.description: "Que cause perigo comum" qualifies only the similar device; any explosive qualifies.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 4º-A — the clause stands next to "artefato análogo"

taken.rationale: An explosive that causes no common danger is hard to picture, so little turns on it. The shared means in cp-dominio records the pair and the clause together, `emprego de explosivo ou de artefato análogo que cause perigo comum`.

notes: The shared means arrives pre-construed, so the encoding cannot exhibit the difference; g4 (crimes of common danger) may want the two apart.

site.anchor: furto qualificado do art. 155, § 5º

source.quote: se a subtração for de veículo automotor que venha a ser transportado para outro Estado ou para o exterior.

readings.description: The vehicle must in fact have been taken across a State border or abroad.
It is enough that the vehicle was taken in order to be carried to another State or abroad.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, § 5º — the subjunctive can be read as purpose

taken.rationale: "Venha a ser transportado" states a result, and a qualifying circumstance is not stretched against the accused. The circumstance is recorded as `veículo transportado para outro Estado ou para o exterior`.

site.anchor: furto consumado (art. 155, caput; art. 14, I)

source.quote: Subtrair, para si ou para outrem, coisa alheia móvel:

readings.description: "Para si ou para outrem" requires taking the thing to keep it as one's own or for another. Taking it to use briefly and give back ("furto de uso") is not theft.

citations.cite: CP art. 155, caput — "para si ou para outrem"

readings.description: Any taking of another's movable thing is theft, whatever the purpose.
readings.rejection_rationale: It reads "para si ou para outrem" out of the text.

taken.rationale: The words are there to be read; the field `para si ou para outrem` asks the fact supplier for that purpose.

site.anchor: atipicidade material pela insignificância

source.quote_absent_reason: The insignificância principle is not in the Code's text; it is a doctrine of the courts about material typicity.

readings.description: A taking that meets the words of the caput is still not a crime where the judge finds it materially insignificant on the STF's four vectors — minimal offensiveness, no social danger, a very low degree of reproach, an inexpressive injury. The encoding takes the finding as an input and never computes it. Return of the thing alone is not enough (STJ Tema 1205), and the principle does not apply to domestic violence against women (Súmula 589 STJ).

citations.cite: STF, HC 84.412/SP (Segunda Turma, rel. Min. Celso de Mello, j. 19.10.2004, DJ 19.11.2004)
STJ, Tema repetitivo 1.205, as reported in sweep-b (M-sweep-b-30)
Súmula 589 STJ, as reported in sweep-b (M-sweep-b-30)

readings.description: The encoding decides theft from the words of the article alone; a trivially small taking is still theft, possibly privileged under § 2º.
Insignificance is computed: the thing is worth at most 10% of the minimum wage at the time of the fact, and the agent is not a repeat offender.

citations.cite: TJDFT, Acórdão 1659805 — a local parameter, as reported in sweep-b (M-sweep-b-30)

readings.foreclosure: A rule of thumb in some state courts with no statutory basis and no binding authority; the STF's test is qualitative, and a figure would replace the judge's assessment.

taken.rationale: The principle is applied by every court, so leaving it out would give answers the courts do not; computing it would replace the judge. As an input finding it keeps the judgement where the courts put it, and the formal predicates (`furto consumado`, `furto tentado`) still state the text alone.

notes: Reserved id: opened by M-sweep-b-30 as F-sweep-b-21; g0 had first written it as F-g0-22, taking the formal reading and encoding nothing. It follows the sweep's suggested reading now.

source.quote: V – lesão corporal grave; ou

citations.cite: CP art. 122, § 1º — "lesão corporal de natureza grave ou gravíssima, nos termos dos §§ 1º e 2º do art. 129"

readings.description: "Lesão corporal grave" covers both grades of art. 129: the grave of § 1º and the gravíssima of § 2º.

citations.cite: CP art. 129, §§ 1º–2º — § 2º's results are heavier than § 1º's, and a provision triggered by the lesser is triggered by the greater

readings.description: "Lesão corporal grave" is only art. 129, § 1º, since the Code names "gravíssima" separately where it means both (art. 122, § 1º).

site.anchor: criança

source.quote: contra criança, adolescente, pessoa maior de 60 (sessenta) anos ou pessoa com deficiência

readings.description: "Criança" is a person under twelve and "adolescente" one from twelve to under eighteen.

citations.cite: Lei nº 8.069/1990 (Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente), art. 2º — outside this encoding's sources, not quoted

site.anchor: a forma admite o privilégio

source.quote: e a qualificadora for de ordem objetiva

readings.description: Abuse of trust (§ 4º, II) and membership of a criminal group (§ 9º) are subjective, being about the agent; every other qualificadora — obstacle, fraud, climbing, sleight of hand, false key, two or more people, the kind of thing, the means — is objective.
Fraud (§ 4º, II; § 4º-B) is subjective too, being about the agent's scheme.

taken.rationale: Fraud describes how the thing was taken, as climbing and sleight of hand do. Abuse of trust and group membership describe who the agent is to the victim or to a group.
